papers.canonical_title: ManimCode: Learning Visual Self-Correction for Educational Animation
papers.abstract: ManimData and ManimCode train a single 4B model to write, review and revise educational-animation programs using render-verified trajectories, role-conditioned supervision and revision reinforcement learning.

events.evidence: Canonical submission history and official Atom metadata agree.

papers.screening_reason: A trained multimodal controller generates and rewrites executable Manim animation programs based on rendered-frame critiques and execution/layout diagnostics.
screening_evidence: Sections 3.2 and 4.2, pp.5–7: deployed 4B model runs render-review-revise loop; Appendix A.3 specifies inference settings.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time scene-level ManimCode render–review–revise subsystem using the SFT+RL 4B backbone. Data construction and training explain adaptation but their 27B reward model is not a deployed verifier; long-form planners are separate integrations.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Writes complete Manim programs, reviews rendered frames, rewrites code and selects the best rendered candidate
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Executable educational-animation scene and its video
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: At inference one 4B model handles all three roles in the render–review–revise loop; each request starts with a generated program and retains the best rendered candidate.

task.evidence: Educational animations explain STEM relationships and processes unfolding over time.
task.reasoning: Temporal educational content is animation; rendering alone is not added as another task.

input_form.evidence: Inference starts from an open request with no reference video or code.

output.evidence: Best candidate program is retained and rendered as the returned video.
output.reasoning: The exposed executable scene program supports Program; returned rendered animation supports Rendered Media.

model_type.evidence: Single Qwen3.5-4B receives request, current program and sampled frames in Reviewer role.
model_type.reasoning: The decision-making backbone directly uses images as well as text, hence VLM.

model_training.evidence: Role-conditioned SFT followed by Reviser RLOO; both stages train LoRA adapters.

planning.evidence: Scene generator writes, reviews and revises code; lecture plans belong to external long-form systems.
planning.reasoning: No explicit multi-step task plan is represented in the analyzed scene-level subsystem. Fixed loop scheduling is workflow, not a planning degree.

workflow.evidence: write, render, review, revise within ten renders.
workflow.reasoning: One ordered refinement path; crash handling is not a substantive hierarchical search.

update_strategy.evidence: Reviser rewrites full program; acceptance keeps improved mean score; revision base returns to best after substantial alignment/completeness degradation.
update_strategy.reasoning: Full-code replacement is Regeneration even for small semantic edits; best retention is Candidate Selection; restoring best as revision base is Rollback.

verifier.locator: Section 3.2 p.5; inference p.7; Appendix A.3 p.15
verifier.evidence: Same 4B backbone reviews frames; layout checker reports geometric defects; renderer returns execution errors.
verifier.reasoning: Shared decision backbone supplies Self; code-based layout checks supply Programmatic; rendering environment supplies Environment. External Gemini final judge is excluded.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Render success/failure, four 1–5 review scores, specific critiques and layout defects guide revisions.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Execution outcome is Binary, review values Score, actionable critique and error explanations Diagnosis.

feedback_observation.evidence: Reviewer sees eight frames; checker reads object positions at pauses; renderer produces errors.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Frames support Visual, object geometry supports Structural Scene State, execution errors support Runtime.

memory_time.evidence: Best and latest candidates retained within each request; request begins with newly generated program.
memory_time.reasoning: Candidate state persists across calls within one generation run, not demonstrated cross-run learning.

memory_reach.evidence: Single backbone plays all roles using current program and feedback; common loop retains best candidate.
memory_reach.reasoning: The shared scene/program state is accessible across the subsystem's roles; no separate private agent stores are asserted.

action_type.evidence: Writer and Reviser output complete executable programs.

graphics_software.evidence: ManimCE is wrapped by render, layout diagnostic and retrieval/refinement loop.
graphics_software.reasoning: Added agent-facing diagnostic/execution adapter over existing Manim; native program API remains the action surface.

tools.evidence: Renderer executes programs; Manim operations animate scenes; layout checker reports overlaps, small labels, off-frame objects.
tools.reasoning: Execution harness is Execution Utilities; native animation operations are Graphics Operations; deterministic geometric checks are Static Validator. Reviewer is not double-counted as a tool.

resources.evidence: Retrieved cards include API documentation, best-practice rules and example scenes; code examples retained verbatim.
resources.reasoning: Rules and API docs support Documentation & Rules; accessed reusable scene examples support Examples & Trajectories, not merely training data.

representation.evidence: Programs render animated text, formulas and diagrams; layout diagnostics inspect positions; reviewer sees frames.
representation.reasoning: Executable programs are Code, structured diagram positions are Layouts, and rendered observations are Pixels.

papers.contribution: Learns the complete animation correction loop in a 4B model from 24,034 quality-filtered trajectories, improving render success to 96.6%/97.0% on two benchmarks.
papers.limitations: Quality gains are smaller than executability gains; revisions can oscillate and leave clipped objects. Human validation uses one blinded team member on 98 pairs; automatic judge agreement is weak for small score gaps. Long-form results use substituted judges and are not directly comparable to published benchmark scores. No dedicated limitations section; these limitations were inspected in Sections 5.4 and Appendix C.
taxonomy_delta: Full-program emission with localized semantic edits is classified Regeneration rather than Local Patch; taxonomy could separately distinguish serialization granularity from edit scope.
Memory uses the snapshot's across-call short-term definition; no cross-run persistence inferred.
Agent-Adapted reflects added diagnostics and execution harness; a narrower interface interpretation could call native Manim code General-Purpose.

papers.canonical_title: CADFather: Autonomous CAD Reconstruction through Coordinated Tool Use
papers.abstract: CADFather coordinates learned operation proposals, algorithmic geometry proposals and numerical parameter optimization to reconstruct editable CAD programs from meshes. A vision-language assistant selects candidate branches, tools and proposal counts using rendered and geometric feedback; models require no additional training.

events.evidence: Canonical v1 submission history; latest and only version shown.

source_records.source: authorized prior pending index; older backlog, not seven-day catch-up

papers.screening_reason: Explicit VLM tool selection changes candidate parametric CAD geometry and controls reconstruction search with feedback.
screening_evidence: Sections 3.1–3.6 pp.3–7 establish candidate/tool decisions, execution, visual acceptance and retained best CAD program.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time CADFather VLM assistant and its bounded candidate-pool reconstruction harness; pretrained CADENA-RL is a proposal tool, not the principal decision model being classified.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Select candidate branch, learned/algorithmic/optimization tool and sample count; accept geometry or finish
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: CadQuery-based executable CAD programs and meshes for a target part
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Assistant issues act calls on named candidates; tools create alternative continuations or refine parameters; executed renders and measurements inform subsequent decisions.

task.evidence: Recover editable CAD model and modeling operations from shape.
task.reasoning: Reconstructing geometric CAD content is Modeling.

output.evidence: Final CAD program + mesh; output is protected best.
output.reasoning: Executable program supports Program; exposed reconstructed mesh supports Graphics Artifact.

model_type.evidence: Qwen3.8-27B assistant inspects target and candidate renders.

model_training.evidence: Both models are frozen; no additional training in system overview.

planning.evidence: One sentence states what the assistant pursues this step, followed by up to four act calls. No multi-step plan state is specified.
planning.reasoning: Reactive candidate/tool decisions and search history do not establish an explicit task plan; generic planning language in limitations is insufficient.

workflow.evidence: Each extension creates a child; assistant can act on multiple candidates and revisit older branches.
workflow.reasoning: Substantive branching search dependencies establish Graph-Structured, not merely a repeated sequential loop.

update_strategy.evidence: Append operations or adjust existing numerical parameters; choose protected best by score.
update_strategy.reasoning: Incremental operation/parameter edits support Local Patch; retaining and returning best supports Candidate Selection. Revisiting immutable alternatives is not asserted to be state rollback.

verifier.evidence: Assistant visually accepts proposals; execution component checks watertightness, positive volume and whether code builds.
verifier.reasoning: Same assistant is Self; geometry checking is Programmatic; CAD execution success/failure is Environment.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Valid/invalid and accept/reject; IoU/GMS score; failed requests return why and available actions.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Validity is Binary; geometric objective is Score; corrective failure explanation is Diagnosis, each used for subsequent calls.

feedback_observation.evidence: Renders, geometric measurements and candidate table, execution failures and timeouts.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Renders are Visual; geometry and pool state Structural Scene State; build/time errors Runtime.

memory_time.evidence: Pool retains earlier candidates for each part; transcript retains executed actions and one-sentence rationales.
memory_time.reasoning: State survives calls for one part; persistent here does not establish cross-part or cross-run memory.

memory_reach.evidence: All tools operate on common pool representation; assistant sees bounded table and execution transcript.
memory_reach.reasoning: Shared per-part state mediates assistant and tools; Global Memory within this system, despite bounded prompt visibility.

action_type.evidence: Assistant answers through act and finish function calls.

graphics_software.evidence: CadQuery DSL exposed through specialized proposal/refinement actions and candidate table.
graphics_software.reasoning: Dedicated agent-facing adapter over CAD execution, not direct native GUI use.

tools.evidence: Operation proposal tools, numerical parameter optimizer, execution and geometry validation.
tools.reasoning: Proposal authoring is Graphics Operations; execution is Execution Utilities; watertight checks Static Validator; optimization explores geometry states and is Solver Validator under provisional codebook.

resources.evidence: Same rule description at every step/part provides task, objective, available tools and cost, answer format.
resources.reasoning: Reusable accessed rules qualify; target mesh is task input, not an asset library.

representation.evidence: Candidate program, generated mesh, and renders.
representation.reasoning: Program is Code; mesh/solid Geometry; rendered observations Pixels.

papers.contribution: Combines complementary CAD proposal and refinement tools under a VLM-controlled candidate search while preserving the best valid reconstruction; evaluates six datasets without additional controller training.
papers.limitations: Restricted operation library and proposal coverage; parameter optimization cannot repair wrong topology. No guarantee of best reconstruction. Evaluation concerns single-part geometry/validity, not manufacturing intent, assemblies or engineering constraints. Ablations do not isolate assistant policy or match consumed compute; API-cost comparisons exclude geometry execution and compare different input modalities/subsets.
taxonomy_delta: Explicit multi-step planning is absent despite generic planning terminology; action rationale is not promoted to PO-3.
Immutable branch revisiting is classified Candidate Selection, not automatically Rollback.
Solver Validator is provisional and here covers numerical CAD fitting rather than physical simulation.

papers.canonical_title: CrowdDirector: Runtime Orchestration of Crowd Simulation through Natural-Language Directives
papers.abstract: CrowdDirector converts new natural-language instructions into validated persistent directives and uses a graph policy to select available actions and targets for virtual agents in Unity, avoiding recurrent language inference.

events.evidence: Canonical history v1 and official metadata. December MIG conference date is future and not counted as publication.

papers.screening_reason: LLM-issued directives patch live scene affordances and a learned graph controller selects actions for animated crowd agents in Unity; controller need not be exclusively an LLM.
screening_evidence: Section 3.2 pp.3–4 specifies scene patches; Sections 3.4 and 3.6 pp.5–7 connect graph-selected actions to Unity movement, interactions and animation.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time hybrid instruction-to-directive and graph-policy runtime crowd orchestration in Unity 2D. Offline rollout/LLM label generation and supervised graph training are described separately, not treated as runtime reward feedback.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: Sparse Claude Haiku instruction interpreter plus recurrent relational GNN policy
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Resolve scene patches and choose action/target candidates for each animated crowd member
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: Running Unity 2D crowd scene, affordances, character motion and interactions
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Validated directives disable affordances, enable alternatives and change attractions; GNN chooses targets, Unity executes movement and animation and reports completion/failure.

task.evidence: Runtime crowd authoring; Unity handles movement, interactions and animation.
task.reasoning: Principal purpose is directing animated crowd behavior, not physical effects simulation.

input_form.evidence: User supplies natural-language directives while scene runs.

output.evidence: Structured directive JSON and selected action/target messages sent to Unity.
output.reasoning: Controller exposes declarative execution instructions, not downloadable code or independently reported video output. Resulting animation is execution effect.

model_type.evidence: Claude Haiku interprets once; relational GNN has no text encoder and repeatedly scores action candidates.
model_type.reasoning: Hybrid composition of language interpreter and non-language graph decision network; no VLM is inferred.

model_training.evidence: Graph network trained with KL and ranking terms on generated labels. No pretrained graph backbone or fine-tuning is stated; interpreter adaptation unspecified.
model_training.reasoning: Supervised training from generated labels is not necessarily Supervised Fine-Tuning. Available labels do not faithfully encode from-scratch graph-policy training; retain Unclear rather than mislabel RL merely because rollouts supply labels.

planning.evidence: Policy selects one candidate; Unity performs path planning and requests next decision after completion/failure.
planning.reasoning: No explicit multi-step controller plan. Low-level engine navigation is not the principal agent plan; author wording replanning refers to selecting a new action.

workflow.evidence: Interpret, validate, build graph/candidates, select, execute.
workflow.reasoning: Ordered pipeline and repeated local loop. Graph is state representation, not evidence of graph-structured scheduling.

update_strategy.evidence: Directives are scene patches; graph policy selects from available actions after updated scene reports.
update_strategy.reasoning: Affordance and attraction changes are Local Patch; decision among listed alternatives is Candidate Selection. No controller plan to revise.

verifier.evidence: Scene validator checks referenced capabilities; partial instructions require user acceptance; Unity reports failure/completion.
verifier.reasoning: Programmatic capability validator gates execution; Human approves partial changes; Environment judges executed outcome. Evaluation participants are not added as loop feedback.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Five feasibility states identify unsupported/ambiguous/invalid instructions; completion/failure triggers new decisions.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Feasibility diagnosis supports Diagnosis; execution outcome supports Binary. Offline rollout scores and final benchmark metrics excluded.

feedback_observation.evidence: Scene graph rebuilt; Unity reports available/reachable entities and action completion/failure.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Entity/affordance state is Structural Scene State; execution status is Runtime. No rendered-frame input to controller.

memory_time.evidence: Directive lifetime 60 ticks; interrupted directive resumes, and newly thirsty agents respond without further LLM call.
memory_time.reasoning: Persistent within a running session across decisions, no cross-run retention established.

memory_reach.evidence: Python holds shared symbolic state; candidate generator and graph policy read all active directives.
memory_reach.reasoning: Scene-level directive memory is shared across crowd decisions, not private to one character.

action_type.evidence: JSON operation and target, then candidate action/target messages interpreted by Unity.
action_type.reasoning: Declarative structured operation specifications rather than emitted scripts or GUI gestures.

graphics_software.evidence: Python symbolic policy connects via WebSocket to Unity 2D scene execution and reports.
graphics_software.reasoning: Dedicated state/action adapter over existing graphics engine.

tools.evidence: Scene validator, runtime operations on affordances and animation, WebSocket execution interface.
tools.reasoning: Validator is Static Validator; scene/animation operations Graphics Operations; dispatch and status exchange Execution Utilities. Offline rollouts are not runtime Solver Validator.

resources.evidence: Fixed operation library and scene type/affordance rules determine supported actions.
resources.reasoning: Reusable simulator rules accessed for action validation qualify Documentation & Rules; live state is not reusable asset retrieval.

representation.evidence: Time-varying needs, active events/operations, Unity 2D zones and object layout.
representation.reasoning: Evolving needs/directives/actions support Dynamic State; 2D spatial scene supports Layouts. Controller consumes no pixels.

papers.contribution: Separates sparse language interpretation from recurrent graph-policy control, storing validated directives as simulation state; reports 20.5 ms versus 3880 ms per decision update on 20-agent worlds.
papers.limitations: Only predefined actions in Unity 2D; 15-person feasibility study and limited scenarios. Policy trained on 8–40 agents; thousands-agent experiment measures computational scaling, not behavioral generalization. Per-tick LLM follows instructions better on several measures. Training labels use fixed blending weights.
taxonomy_delta: Codebook lacks supervised-from-scratch graph-controller training; Unclear preserves mismatch instead of falsely assigning SFT or RL.
Hybrid includes LLM plus graph-policy controller. If Hybrid is intended only for LLM/VLM combinations, taxonomy needs a non-language controller category.
No explicit controller plan; low-level engine path planning and reactive next-action selection are kept separate.

papers.canonical_title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
papers.abstract: A 100-instance expert-curated SVG motion-editing benchmark pairs each prompt with a deterministic verification program. A writer and test synthesizer construct verifiers through iteration over human-labeled animations and generated transformations; evaluation covers 47 model configurations.

events.evidence: Official metadata and canonical v1 history.

papers.screening_reason: The verifier-construction subsystem includes an agent that writes deterministic transformations on actual animation artifacts and repairs cases on challenge, coupled to a verifier-writing agent. Final generation benchmark itself is independent one-shot sampling, not an iterative editing agent.
screening_evidence: Section 4.2 p.6; Appendix B.2 pp.16–17: synthesizer changes timing, direction, extent, position, appearance and SVG structure and repairs challenged test cases.
papers.analysis_target: Data-generation/evaluation-construction phase: GPT-6 Astra verifier writer plus animation test-case synthesizer. The separately evaluated GSAP generators do not consume verifier feedback; their final pass@k metrics are not the classified loop.

agent_graphics_relation.controller: GPT-6 Astra test-case synthesizer coordinated with verifier writer
agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Writes deterministic transformations of valid animations; upholds, repairs or replaces challenged test cases
agent_graphics_relation.graphics_target: SVG-frame animation test artifacts and their motion/appearance properties
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: Synthesizer uses transformation library on source or approved animations; writer challenges each generated slot at most once with prompt clause and measured evidence; synthesizer repairs/replaces cases.

task.evidence: Tests exercise animation motion timing, direction, extent and appearance.
task.reasoning: Audit construction concerns temporal vector animation.

input_form.evidence: Prompt, static SVG/PNG, source Lottie and labeled animations provided.
input_form.reasoning: Motion request is Language; static vector and PNG reference Image; temporal animations Video. Structured SVG code noted in representation.

output.evidence: Run returns one verification program per benchmark instance.

model_type.evidence: Both agents GPT-6 Astra; writer inputs include PNG and animation evidence.
model_type.reasoning: Multimodal decision model consumes visual artifact inputs; not inferred from commercial model name alone.

model_training.locator: Section 4.2 and Appendix B.2; full-text training search
model_training.evidence: Model identities and prompts reported, adaptation/training of construction agents not specified.
model_training.reasoning: Named commercial use does not prove Off-the-Shelf; no explicit adaptation statement after full text and appendix review.

planning.evidence: Writer/synthesizer iterative protocol and case review, without explicit multi-step task plan state.
planning.reasoning: Fixed protocol is workflow, not evidence of a planning representation.

workflow.evidence: Writer tests complete example set; independent synthesizer withholds candidate reports; disagreement branches to case review before further revision.
workflow.reasoning: Interdependent writer/test-generation and conditional challenge dependencies support Graph-Structured; not claim of parallel execution.

update_strategy.evidence: Writer resubmits complete revised program; synthesizer repairs or replaces challenged cases while keeping label and slot.
update_strategy.reasoning: Complete candidate resubmission/replacement supports Regeneration; targeted case transformation repair supports Local Patch.

verifier.evidence: Programmatic checks and labels determine disagreement; writer challenges synthesized case with evidence, synthesizer reviews it.
verifier.reasoning: Execution/classification checks are Programmatic; other role's challenge is Critic. Human labels are previously supplied resources, not online human verifier.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Pass/fail per check with measurements; challenges cite prompt clauses and missing/overly strict checks.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Binary outcomes and Diagnosis affect program/test repair. Held-out agreement scores are not feedback.

feedback_observation.evidence: Reports contain measured SVG geometry and temporal attributes plus execution errors.
feedback_observation.reasoning: Measurements are Structural Scene State; execution errors Runtime. Visual inputs are not independently documented as loop observations.

memory_time.evidence: Earlier synthesized-case descriptions, persistent case slots and complete example set retained for each instance.
memory_time.reasoning: Per-instance cross-call retention is Short-Term Memory; final verifier artifact is not itself long-term agent memory.

memory_reach.evidence: Synthesizer receives prior case descriptions but not writer's candidate or reports.
memory_reach.reasoning: Deliberate role-specific information isolation supports Local Memory; not all state is shared.

action_type.evidence: Writer emits Python checks; synthesizer writes deterministic transformations using supplied library.

graphics_software.evidence: MoVer/Chromium execution, animation matrix and dedicated transformation/verification libraries.
graphics_software.reasoning: Specialized agent-facing layer over existing browser/vector animation tooling.

tools.evidence: Transformation library changes animation properties; execution engine runs tests; verifier measures/checks animation matrix.
tools.reasoning: Transformations Graphics Operations; runner Execution Utilities; deterministic temporal/geometry checks Static Validator (not an optimizing solver).

resources.evidence: Source Lottie and SVG; human-labeled construction animations and notes; supplied libraries/tool catalogs and worked examples.
resources.reasoning: Source artwork Assets; approved/rejected exemplars Examples & Trajectories; library contracts and safeguards Documentation & Rules.

representation.evidence: Python programs, SVG geometry/hierarchy, motion attributes across frames, PNG input.
representation.reasoning: Python is Code; SVG structure Layouts; temporal matrix Dynamic State; supplied PNG Pixels.

papers.contribution: Constructs auditable prompt-specific temporal verifiers through multi-agent test synthesis; achieves 93.3% agreement on 180 held-out animations versus 83.3% for the VLM baseline.
papers.limitations: 100 moderate-complexity instances, long detailed prompts and GSAP-specific generation evaluation; lacks large scenes, complex deformation and multi-turn interaction. Nine false rejections and three false approvals on held-out data; initial annotator agreement cannot be reconstructed. Iterative correction of evaluated generators remains future work.
taxonomy_delta: Task-time benchmark is non-iterative; core classification rests on demonstrated animation transformations in the principal verifier-construction agent subsystem, not imagined runtime feedback.
Model-training label remains Not Reported despite named commercial agent.

papers.canonical_title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
papers.abstract: LongBanana provides 90 expert-designed multi-reference image synthesis tasks and 4,670 atomic checks. It studies direct, minimal harness and ReAct–Plan–Exec–Reflect generation, plus an independently validated agentic checklist judge.

events.evidence: Official Atom published/updated v1 timestamp; canonical page identifies sole v1.

papers.screening_reason: Generation harness selects evidence, decomposes prompts, calls image backend, inspects drafts and revises image-generation requests.
screening_evidence: Section 4.1 p.7 and Appendix D.2 p.36 explicitly connect controller decisions to generated image drafts and repairs.
papers.analysis_target: Task-time LongBanana-Gen OpenClaw+RPR with Claude Sonnet 4.6 controlling Nano Banana 2. The separate Gemini checklist evaluator and privileged graph baseline are not mixed into this taxonomy.

agent_graphics_relation.action_or_decision: Select references, build prompt schedule, invoke image generation/editing and revise after draft review
agent_graphics_relation.locator: Section 4.1 p.7; Appendix C.1 p.33; D.2 p.36
agent_graphics_relation.evidence: ReAct retrieves evidence, Plan–Exec decomposes request into generation/edit steps, Reflect inspects drafts and decides retrieval/revision; final synthesized image exposed.

task.evidence: Compose entities, appearance and relations into one coherent image.
task.reasoning: Image composition/content creation mapped conservatively to Modeling; not scientific data Visualization and not animation despite temporal-state reasoning tasks. Taxonomy boundary flagged.

input_form.evidence: User instruction and reference set with distractors; agent receives neither hidden graph nor evaluation checklist.

output.reasoning: Exposed raster output is Rendered Media; internal schedule is not extra output.

model_type.locator: Appendix C.1 p.33 and D.2 p.36
model_type.evidence: Sonnet agent observes references and reviews visual drafts.
model_type.reasoning: Controller uses images and language, hence VLM rather than classifying pixel backend.

model_training.locator: Appendix C.1 p.33; full-text adaptation search
model_training.evidence: Shared model/harness versions reported, no explicit training or adaptation procedure for controller.
model_training.reasoning: Named model use alone does not establish Off-the-Shelf; Not Reported after full text including reproducibility checklist.

planning.evidence: Fixed RPR stages; agent decomposes subgoals and builds scene plan/prompt schedule.
planning.reasoning: Explicit model-built plan within hard-coded staged scaffolding supports PO-2.

workflow.evidence: RPR described as serial ReAct, Plan–Exec, Reflect workflow with repair loop.

update_strategy.evidence: Detect missing content/wrong bindings; revise prompts and repair by further generation/editing.
update_strategy.reasoning: Repeated pixel backend calls from revised requests support Regeneration; no localized patch API or explicit revised plan documented.

verifier.evidence: Agent-directed draft review uses shared Sonnet agent; separate Gemini judge scores final outputs.
verifier.reasoning: Self reflection is demonstrated inside generation. Do not import final evaluation critic or human annotators as loop verifier.

feedback_assessment.evidence: Missing content and wrong bindings guide prompt revision.
feedback_assessment.reasoning: Defect detection is Diagnosis; benchmark checklist scores are withheld and not loop Score.

feedback_observation.evidence: Reflect inspects draft images before deciding repairs.

memory_time.evidence: Harness maintains reference state and revisions; shared agent state feeds repair loop.
memory_time.reasoning: Cross-stage within-request retention supports Short-Term Memory, no cross-run reuse established.

memory_reach.evidence: Shared agent state spans ReAct, Plan–Exec and Reflect.
memory_reach.reasoning: State shared across analyzed stages supports Global Memory.

action_type.evidence: Harness calls reference browsing, image-generation, file and prompt-management tools.

graphics_software.evidence: OpenClaw wraps fixed image backend with references and revision state.
graphics_software.reasoning: Agent harness adapts image-generation interface rather than native graphics GUI.

tools.evidence: Image backend produces pixels; reference browsing and file/prompt management called by agent.
tools.reasoning: Generative backend fits provisional Perception models label (analyze or generate); file/prompt management Execution Utilities. Judge-only verification tools not imported.

resources.evidence: Inventory of reference object/style/background images reused across stages.
resources.reasoning: Accessed image content is Assets; no hidden graph/checklist as runtime rule resource.

representation.evidence: References, intermediate drafts and final image; prompt schedule is controller state.
representation.reasoning: Graphics content is Pixels. Text plan does not establish explicit editable geometry/layout representation.

papers.contribution: Provides dense reference-grounded synthesis evaluation and shows adaptive harness gains over graph-privileged static staging; OpenClaw+RPR reaches 78.4 overall versus 74.6 for PD-Direct.
papers.limitations: Only 90 high-density image cases, not 3D/video. RPR gains depend on harness and can cause drift; task pass rates decline for some variants. Judge still has 24.81% opposite-end item errors. Reproduction commands, environment files, runtime and API costs are absent; abstract release claims conflict with checklist saying no public executable access instructions.
taxonomy_delta: Raster composition task mapped to Modeling; source examples do not fully settle Modeling versus Visualization for general 2D image synthesis.
Generator and evaluator must remain separate: final checklist scores are not generator feedback, and evaluation graph is unavailable to the agent.
